svg.title: Step 5 · Our own graph
svg.desc: The agent is a LangGraph graph of our own. Its state holds the conversation and the number of calls to the model. The model node calls Gemini with the tools, or, at the fifth call, with calling them turned off, so every answer ends in words; each call's first words must come within 10 seconds. The route sends each tool call the model asked for to the tools node as a task of its own, or ends the run on words. The tools node runs each call within 8 seconds and returns the result to the model. The whole answer stays within 30 seconds.
svg.text: Step 5 · Our own graph
The same loop as step 4's, its limits now in our code
AgentState
messages: the conversation, each node's messages added to it · model_calls: the calls to the model so far
START
"model": call_model()
① model_calls + 1; the tools bound with tool_choice "auto",
or "none" at the fifth call: an answer always ends in words
the first words within 10 s, or the answer ends as too slow
each chunk to the page as it comes, via LangGraph
② route(): after each call to the model
tool calls: Send("tools", [call]) for each, a task of its own
words, no tool call: the end of the run
the fifth call has no tools: it always ends here
END: words
"tools": LangGraph's ToolNode, one call a task
each of our four tools, within 8 s, its tries included
a failure: our sentence, as a tool error
each result to the state, and its chip ends
then the model
again
The limits: 5 calls to the model · 10 s for each call's first words · 8 s a tool call · 30 s the answer
The loop's limits are the agent's real rules: they belong in our code, where tests hold them.
The page, the tools and the logs are step 4's: only the loop changed hands.
